headline: Holgate's Outer Bar Split In Two — Blues Inside, Fluke On The New Drop
subhead: A summer swell carved a fresh slough off Holgate and the bite followed it — here's where to fish it and what's biting from the inlet to the Mullica.
body_markdown:
I walked the Holgate stretch Tuesday morning at dead low and something's different out there. The outer bar that's held its shape since June split into two distinct humps, with a new trough running maybe forty yards off the beach where there used to be one continuous shelf. You can see it from the dune line if the sun's low enough — darker water in the cut, lighter sand color on the inside bar. That kind of split usually means one thing: baitfish get funneled into that new trough and whatever's hunting them stacks up right on the edge of it. I fished the drop-off on the incoming Wednesday morning with a bone-colored darter and picked up three bluefish in the 3-4 pound class in maybe twenty minutes before the sun got too high and pushed them off the structure.

That's been the story on bluefish all summer and it hasn't slowed down — steady action, mostly 3 to 4 pounders with the occasional 6 to 8 pound fish mixed in, and it's holding both in the surf and inside. Snapper blues are thick right now in the back bay and river mouths — Graveling Point, the mouth of the Mullica, up into Great Bay proper. If you've got kids who want bent rods, small silver spoons or Kastmasters off the bulkheads at Beach Haven or the Causeway bridges will keep them busy for hours. We flagged a couple weeks back that the snapper density was a signal adult blues would keep building through late August into September, and that's exactly what's playing out — the adult fish mixing into those bunker pods along the beachfront are bigger on average than they were in July.

Fluke is the real story on LBI right now, though, and it's genuinely good. Boats running out of Barnegat Light and Beach Haven are posting 4, 5, even 7-keeper trips this week on structure — the reef sites, rock piles off the inlet, and the humps along the Barnegat Ridge. The pattern that's working is oversized baits fished tight to bottom: 6-inch chartreuse or pink Gulp grubs on 3/4 to 1-ounce bucktails, tipped with a whole squid strip or a chunk of mackerel. If you're fishing structure and you're not occasionally ticking bottom, you're fishing too high — these fish are lazy in this warm water and they want the bait dropped right on their head, not swimming past twelve inches over them.

Bay-side, the pattern's shifted with the heat. The shallow flats in Great Bay and up toward Graveling Point are running warm — upper 70s pushing 80 in the skinny water — and that's pushed fluke out of the marsh edges and concentrated them right at the mouth of Little Egg Inlet, where the tidal exchange keeps water cooler and better oxygenated. Anchor up on the edge of the main channel there on the last two hours of the ebb and drift live spot or a Gulp Swimming Mullet on a light jighead through the current seam. That's where the keepers are sitting right now, not out on the open flats.

Striped bass are a tougher conversation. The warm water in the bay and along the beachfront has compressed the bite into tight dawn and dusk windows, same as everywhere south of the Canyon country right now. We called this exact pattern back on August 7 — said the bass bite would hold steady until temps ease off in September, and that building tidal flow into the new moon would sharpen things up at current-driven structure. That's precisely what's happening. First light at Barnegat Light around the rocks, and again at the Holgate cuts on that new trough I mentioned, has been giving up slot fish mixed with the bluefish, mostly on darters and 5-inch soft plastic swimbaits worked slow along the bottom edge. By 7:30 or so the window's closed and it turns into a bluefish morning. Don't expect consistency — it's a couple fish in a tight hour, not a blitz.

Kingfish have been showing in the wash at Surf City and Ship Bottom early, before the beaches fill in — small stuff on bloodworm or Fishbites bounced along the sandy troughs close to shore, a nice light-tackle diversion if you're out there anyway for the bass window. Weakfish I'll be honest with you — scattered at best. A few fish showing on soft plastics in the evening up in the Mullica and around Graveling Point, but nothing you can plan a trip around right now. If you connect, it's a bonus, not a target.

Looking ahead, the moon's building back toward the August 28 full, and that added tidal push should sharpen the current at every cut and inlet mouth we've talked about here — Little Egg, Barnegat Inlet, that new Holgate trough. If the swell stays modest through the weekend I'd expect that structure to keep producing on the fluke side and the bass window to hold its shape at first light. Keep an eye on that Holgate cut, too — these things move fast in August, and by Labor Day it could look completely different again. The mullet run's still a few weeks out, but when the peanut bunker start showing thick in the wash off Holgate, that's usually the tell that the real fall pattern is about to switch on.
